description:
Check a schema.org JSON-LD object before it ships: the top-level node, every @graph node, and the nested items engines read (FAQPage Question/acceptedAnswer.text, BreadcrumbList ListItem position/name/item, HowTo steps, Product offers/aggregateRating/review, addresses). Each issue has a property path such as mainEntity[0].acceptedAnswer.text.

Billing: free — local check, no network, no LLM tokens.

Types: Article, BlogPosting, HowTo, FAQPage, Product, Organization, BreadcrumbList, WebSite, SoftwareApplication, Service, LocalBusiness, WebPage, Person, and their subtypes (NewsArticle, Corporation, Plumber, WebApplication…). @type arrays use the first known type; a wrong-case @type gets a 'did you mean' and is still checked.

Checks: @context must be schema.org (http/https, trailing slash, array or @vocab object all fine); URLs must be absolute with a real domain (no relative paths or @handles); ISO 8601 dates and durations; availability/itemCondition enums; ISO 4217 currencies; plain-number prices; Product needs offers, review or aggregateRating. Misspelled properties (e.g. adress) are warnings.

When to call: before every wp_set_post_schema / wp_set_organization_schema / wp_set_faq_schema write, and on any hand-edited JSON-LD. generate_schema already returns this result.

Returns: { valid, type, checked_types, issues: [{ severity: error|warning|info, property, message }], suggestions, suggested_next?, next_step? } (suggested_next: a valid Organization or WebSite node with one paired WordPress site → wp_set_organization_schema, priced). Fix every error and re-validate before writing. Each message says whether a requirement comes from Google's rich-result guides or from AuditAE (schema.org itself requires nothing). Suggestions are optional properties with the reason each matters.

payload.description: The full JSON-LD object, including @context and @type (or a @graph array).

name: validate_schema
title: Validate a schema.org JSON-LD payload against the AuditAE-supported types
